headline: What to Do Immediately After a Hit-and-Run Accident?
articleBody: It's a frightening moment: you've been in an accident, and the other driver just takes off. Your first priority is always safety. Make sure you and any passengers are okay and move to a safe location if possible. Even though the other driver fled, gathering as much information as you can right away is crucial for your potential claim. Try to remember everything you can about the vehicle that hit you – make, model, color, any identifying features, and especially the license plate number, even if it's just a partial one. Don't chase the other driver; it's too dangerous. Instead, call 911 immediately to report the incident to the police. They'll create an official report, which is vital for insurance claims and any future legal action. While waiting for the authorities, look around for witnesses who might have seen what happened and ask for their contact information. If you have a phone, take pictures or videos of the accident scene, including your vehicle's damage, road conditions, and any relevant surroundings. The more detail you can capture, the better. And definitely, don't admit fault or apologize to anyone at the scene. Once you're safe and have gathered initial information, contacting a personal injury attorney, like Brett Peterson in San Diego, can help you understand your rights and guide you through the next steps, especially when dealing with the complexities of a hit-and-run.
